picks.style: ancient greek tragedy, kithara and low aulos, solo female voice over dark drone, grave, unhurried
picks.why: Deianeira's opening: the river-god suitor who came as bull, as coiled serpent, as ox-faced man with springwater in his beard.

picks.style: ancient greek tragic monody, aulos and heavy frame drum, anguished baritone, keening chorus, slow building to violent
picks.why: Heracles begging Hades for sleep, then counting the labours that could not kill him against the woman who did.

picks.style: ancient greek monody, lyre and soft aulos, high female voice with birdlike melisma, longing, gentle, slow
picks.why: The halcyon chorus — 'I, wingless bird that I am, compare my laments with yours' — homesickness turned into birdsong.

picks.style: greek chorus with anatolian colour, aulos, frame drum, layered female voices, keening, ritual, slow
picks.why: Libations of milk, wine and the labour of the tawny bees, answered by a barbarian cry of Asian hymns for the fallen Atreidae.

picks.style: delphic hymn, kithara and lyre, mixed chorus, modal, processional, mysterious
picks.why: Earth breeding dream-visions to steal prophecy back from Apollo, and Zeus smiling as the child clutches his throne.

picks.style: roman hymn, lyre and low flutes, warm male soloist with chorus, flowing, radiant, moderate
picks.why: The invocation of Venus — the most famous opening in Latin verse, and pure incantatory repetition: 'For thee... for thee...'.

picks.style: epicurean meditation, plucked lyre over soft drone, calm baritone, slow, consoling
picks.why: Life given to none in fee-simple, only in usufruct; death as a mirror of the time before we were born, serener far than sleep.

picks.style: latin philosophical chant, steady hand drums, sparse strings, level male voice, hypnotic, mid-tempo
picks.why: The swerve — atoms falling like raindrops through the unbottomed void until one of them declines a little.

picks.style: greek war-hymn chorus, bronze bells and frame drums, layered male voices, driving, exultant
picks.why: 'Thou Rider golden and swift and sheer, Achilles falters: appear! appear!' — rhymed, chanting, made for a chorus.

picks.style: greek lament, solo mezzo over drone, sparse lyre, keening, slow, curse-refrain
picks.why: The Muse mourning her son and cursing Odysseus, Diomede and Helen who emptied a thousand cities of good men.

picks.style: hymn to apollo, kithara and aulos, mixed chorus, luminous, processional, steady
picks.why: Apollo's music rolling stone on stone to raise young Ilion into towers of light — one clean image, well-shaped.

picks.style: late roman chant, sparse lyre and low drone, single male voice, chain-refrain, hypnotic, slow
picks.why: The chained verse: Chance to Hope to Death to Night to Light to Sun — each word handed to the next, a built-in refrain.

picks.style: german romantic ode, strings and piano, soaring tenor with rising chorus, exalted, building
picks.why: 'Lifeless masses are we, when we hate; Gods, when we cling' — the ladder from savage to seraph, dancing until time itself sinks.

picks.style: german art song turning to chorale, piano and horns, ardent tenor, warm, quickening
picks.why: 'Happy! happy! I have found thee... Let the wild chaos return' — friendship set against the collapse of the atoms.

picks.style: mock-oracular chant, aulos drone and finger cymbals, sonorous male voice, solemn with a sardonic edge, slow
picks.why: The fake Sibylline oracle for Peregrinus' pyre — hexameters that sound holy and end on fifteen talents of usury.

picks.style: ancient greek epic recitation, kithara over soft drone, warm male voice, calm, mysterious, slow
picks.why: Only candidate, and a good one: the gods walking as strangers from afar to watch the violence and good order of men.
